items.title: Released isn't Realized

From the Scrum Guide: "Each element of the framework serves a specific purpose that is essential to the overall value and results realized with Scrum." The Cambridge Dictionary defines realize as "to achieve things you hope for or plan for." Hold that against how teams usually count. They plan an item, build it, release it and call it done. items.title: What Do You Want to Learn in 2027?

So, I put together six questions that take about 2 minutes. They ask about your role, where your organization stands with AI, what you want to improve, and how you prefer to learn. items.title: The loudest voice already won before you sat down.
items.excerpt: Image You know this meeting. The data is right there on the screen. Then the most senior person in the room says what they think, and the decision quietly bends to match, evidence or no evidence. Or it's the other version: someone frames the question in the first thirty seconds, a couple of people nod, and the room "agrees," while three people who saw it differently decide this isn't the moment to say so.
